narrative.summary: Kyrgyzstan regulates AI through Chapter 23 of its Digital Code (Code No. 178 of 31 July 2025, in force from early 2026), a risk-based regime under which owners assess the hazard of their AI systems, AI systems of increased danger need a declaration of conformity, and interactions with AI and deepfakes must be disclosed; the Code replaced the 2008 personal information law. Key official websites (the legislation database and the digital ministry) could not be accessed during this review, so the Cabinet's implementing rules on AI hazard assessment, a draft AI ethics regulation and the draft AI development concept could not be read.
lead_institutions: State Agency for Personal Data Protection
narrative.review_notes: This review was completed on 12 October 2026 and covers national law, government, ministries and regulators. The national legislation database and the digital ministry's website could not be accessed, so only two documents could be read in full and several AI rules and drafts are listed as leads. Kyrgyzstan is marked for a later retry.

instruments.english_title: Digital Code of the Kyrgyz Republic
instruments.issuing_authority: Jogorku Kenesh of the Kyrgyz Republic (Code of 31 July 2025 No. 178, signed by the President)
instruments.current_status: Code of 31 July 2025 No. 178 (edition of 31.07.2025 on the Ministry of Justice legal database). Law of 31 July 2025 No. 179 "On bringing into force the Digital Code" (adopted by the Jogorku Kenesh 18 June 2025, published in Erkin-Too of 5 August 2025 No. 58) brings the Code into force six months after that publication, i.e. from early February 2026 (no exact day stated, so effective_date is left null), and repeals among others the Law "On personal information" of 14 April 2008 No. 58, the Law "On electronic governance" and the Law "On electronic signature". The Cabinet of Ministers must set hazard-assessment requirements and the declaration form for AI systems; a Cabinet resolution of 2 December 2025 doing so is held as a lead. A Kyrgyz-language official version exists on the same database.
instruments.summary: Code of 31 July 2025 No. 178 consolidating rules on the digital environment, digital services and systems, digital identity, personal data and telecommunications. Chapter 23 (Articles 191-197) sets principles for AI systems (risk reduction, openness, explainability, human control, accuracy, reliability, security), prohibits AI designed to deliberately and unlawfully harm protected interests, and requires every owner to assess the danger of its AI system and publish the result and methodology. Owners of "increased-danger" AI systems must run lifecycle risk management, keep documentation and logs and sign a published conformity declaration before use (requirements and declaration form set by the Cabinet of Ministers); users must ensure human oversight and explain AI-assisted decisions affecting rights, and providers must disclose AI interactions, emotion-recognition/biometric categorisation and deepfakes.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: First binding horizontal AI rules (the Code also replaced the 2008 Law on personal information and created a special-regulation sandbox regime) in Kyrgyzstan: risk-based duties for owners and users of AI systems, transparency and deepfake labelling.

instruments.summary: Kyrgyzstan's first personal data protection law (No. 58 of 14 April 2008, as amended in 2017 and 2021), regulating the collection, processing and use of personal data by state bodies, local governments and legal entities on the basis of international principles. It set rules for personal data arrays and their holders, data subject rights and cross-border transfer, and barred merging personal data arrays collected for different purposes for automated processing. It was repealed by Law No. 179 of 31 July 2025 when the Digital Code (Chapter 11 on personal data) entered into force.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: Former general data protection law that governed AI training and use on personal data until replaced by the Digital Code.
